description: PyFlowline is a Python tool for generating conceptual river networks on different hydrological-model meshes. The repository describes flowline simplification, mesh generation or import, and reconstruction of network topology from flowline-mesh intersections. It supports structured grids as well as user-provided unstructured meshes and uses GeoJSON in its mesh workflow. These outputs can prepare river-routing representations that feed reservoir, water-supply or flood simulations. The tool is geographically portable; the source vectors and mesh determine spatial detail. Source code and quick-start documentation are publicly available through GitHub under BSD-3-Clause. NumPy, GDAL and netCDF4 are documented dependencies. A limitation is that simplifying braided or otherwise complex flowlines changes network representation, so the resulting topology requires application-specific checks. No directly related catalogue record was established, and compatibility with an arbitrary hydrological solver is not implied. This review read metadata and documentation without generating a mesh or downloading river-network data. The code is available free of charge under its stated licence.
